claims.claim: **ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion**: isolated thrombocytopenia in a well child with no concerning features and an otherwise normal FBE and film. There is no confirmatory test, and other causes of petechiae and purpura must be excluded.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Decide on treatment from clinical features, not the platelet count; most children need none.** The risk of intracranial haemorrhage is very low (under 1%).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Newly diagnosed ITP** is most common at 2–6 years, often follows a viral infection, starts suddenly, is typically self-limiting and usually recovers within 3–6 months. **Persistent** = 3–12 months; **chronic** = over 12 months, seen more often in adolescents (20–30%).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Typical story:** sudden petechial rash and easy bruising in an often well-looking child; epistaxis, gum, GI bleeding, haematuria or menorrhagia; a preceding viral infection or recent live vaccine (e.g. MMR).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intracranial haemorrhage is rare (under 1%)**: headache, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, irritability, reduced consciousness or neurological symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags for another diagnosis:** limp, bone pain, weight loss, anorexia, fever, jaundice, sweats or infection · rash, arthritis, myalgia, dry eyes, mouth ulcers, recurrent infections · family or personal bleeding history · recent NSAIDs, anticoagulants or antiplatelet drugs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials:** leukaemia · bacterial or viral infection · inflicted injury · marrow disorders such as aplastic anaemia · SLE · drug-induced thrombocytopenia · TTP or HUS · localised SVC-distribution petechiae after vomiting or Valsalva.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **0** none · **1 minor**: 100 or fewer petechiae and/or 5 or fewer small bruises (3 cm or less), no mucosal bleeding · **2 mild**: over 100 petechiae and/or over 5 bruises over 3 cm.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **3a (moderate, low risk)**: nares with blood in them, painless oral purpura, petechiae on the palate or in the mouth, buccal purpura only along the molars, epistaxis 5 minutes or less · **3b moderate, high risk**: epistaxis over 5 minutes, haematuria, haematochezia, painful oral purpura, significant menorrhagia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **4 (severe)**: suspected internal haemorrhage (brain, lung, muscle, joint) or mucosal bleeding · **5 (life-threatening)**: bleeding anywhere that threatens life, or documented ICH.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FBE and blood film are the only initial tests needed**; the film must be reviewed to exclude another diagnosis, and other tests are targeted to the differential or complications.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment aims to halt active bleeding — a normal platelet count is not the target.** Weigh active bleeding, future bleeding risk (e.g. impending surgery) and psychosocial factors.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low risk (grades 0–3a): outpatient, no medical treatment** unless there are significant safety or psychosocial concerns; **review with a repeat FBE after 1 week**, and educate the family.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate (3b): often needs admission.** A haematologist must review or discuss the film before treatment starts; raise the platelet count enough to stop bleeding, not to normal.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First line: 4–7 days of prednisolone by mouth, 2–4 mg/kg (max 100 mg).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second line** (poor response, or a rapid rise needed, e.g. before surgery): **IVIg 0.8–1 g/kg**, discussed with Haematology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For epistaxis, tranexamic acid by mouth 25 mg/kg (max 1.5 g)**, possibly with ENT; heavy menstrual bleeding is also listed for additional treatment. ⚠️ **Never give tranexamic acid if there is haematuria.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe (4)** — suspected internal haemorrhage or mucosal bleeding needing immediate intervention: **urgent Haematology consultation; IVIg 0.8–1 g/kg together with IV pulse methylprednisolone for 3 days, 30 mg/kg (max 1 g) each day.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Also in severe bleeding: transfuse platelets 20 mL/kg** (continuously if required) · **tranexamic acid IV, 15 mg/kg (max 1–1.5 g)** · thrombopoietin receptor agonists (romiplostim or eltrombopag) if life-threatening · urgent surgery or referral depending on the bleeding site.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haematology consultation for:** life-threatening or severe bleeding · age under 1 or over 14 · any film abnormality · any concern for another diagnosis · chronic ITP · signs of ICH or a head injury.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give written information and a letter documenting the diagnosis.** Restrict activities to limit head injury: **no contact sports** (football, rugby, soccer, hockey, martial arts); limit horse-riding, skiing, scooters, skateboards, bikes, climbing equipment and trampolines. **Any head injury: present to ED.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid antiplatelet drugs, NSAIDs, anticoagulants and intramuscular injections.** Significant bleeding or signs of ICH need emergency department review.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** for diagnostic uncertainty, red flags, follow-up arrangements, or concern about the family's ability to follow the plan. Ongoing care: Haematology, General Paediatrics or GP depending on context.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer** for severe or life-threatening haemorrhage or care beyond the local service. **Discharge when the family understands** the condition, restrictions and when to go to ED, with a **specific follow-up plan including when to repeat the FBE.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Immune thrombocytopenic purpura' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Immune_thrombocytopenic_purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23
